rule: Deferred task instances must be counted toward `max_active_tis_per_dag`/`max_active_tis_per_dagrun` maps but excluded from the DAG-run active-tasks map that backs `max_active_tasks`, and any divergence between the three limits must be justified in a comment

rationale: `max_active_tasks` bounds tasks occupying executor slots, and deferred tasks hold no slot; the per-task limits bound concurrency of the task itself, so the asymmetry is deliberate and must be spelled out or reviewers will read it as a bug

rule: Conditions that are expected during normal scheduler races must not be logged at WARNING inside methods the scheduler loop re-runs every iteration; use DEBUG/INFO or aggregate the message

rationale: The scheduler re-runs these helpers continuously; a WARNING on a row that is not consumed repeats forever and drowns real warnings during ordinary operation

rule: When the scheduler and a UI/API route both select a single record from the same pending-work table, both must apply the same ordering so the UI shows the row the scheduler will actually act on
trigger: A scheduler query adds `.order_by(<Model>.created_at)` (FIFO) over a pending table such as `AssetPartitionDagRun` while a route under `api_fastapi/core_api/routes/ui/` selects the same table with `.order_by(...created_at.desc()).limit(1)`
rationale: Divergent ordering makes the UI report progress for one partition key while the scheduler fires a different one, and users cannot tell why the run they were watching is not the one that started

rule: Trigger/orphan cleanup queries must express "no referencing row" with a correlated `~exists(select(Child.trigger_id).where(Child.trigger_id == Trigger.id))` rather than `Trigger.id.not_in(select(...))`, and must not carry a redundant `is_not(None)` inside the EXISTS
trigger: A scheduler/triggerer cleanup query filters unreferenced `Trigger` rows with `not_in(select(...))` over a nullable FK column, or a new referencing table is added to that filter
rationale: `NOT IN` over a nullable column silently returns nothing once any referenced row is NULL; the correlated `NOT EXISTS` form is NULL-safe, and reviewers verified both forms produce identical results before the change landed

rule: Alembic data migrations must not do per-row work over a whole table: batch UPDATEs into one `conn.execute(update().where(bindparam(...)), [rows])` and stage join keys into a temporary column instead of running a correlated join per row

rationale: Migrations run once on production deployments with very large tables; a round-trip per row turns a 10k-row table into 10k statements and stretches upgrade downtime, and the codebase already has a bulk-bindparam precedent to copy

rule: A uniqueness invariant that a new ORM model's docstring asserts must be enforced by a database constraint, not by a comment plus a "work on the latest row" fallback

rationale: Without the constraint the scheduler can create duplicate pending rows and then act on an arbitrary one; the guard belongs in the schema where concurrent writers cannot bypass it
